findings.question: Which work regime was agreed for the disputed period (January 2026)?
findings.reason: Approved contract_change REC-0001 (100%) is valid until 2026-02-28; the approved amendment REC-0002 (70%) only starts on 2026-03-01.

findings.question: Which work regime did payroll process for January 2026?
findings.reason: payroll_input REC-0004 (processed) uses 70%; it is derived from HR master data REC-0003 (70% from 2026-01-01), so both count as one origin.

findings.question: Does the processed regime match the agreed regime?
findings.reason: Agreed 100% (REC-0001) vs processed 70% (REC-0004). The HR master data effective date 2026-01-01 precedes the amendment's effective date 2026-03-01.

findings.question: Is the paid amount explained?
findings.reason: Full-time reference salary 5000 gross (REC-0001) x processed regime 70% = 3500, equal to base_salary_gross_paid on payslip REC-0005 and to the amount the client reported.

findings.question: Could unpaid absence explain the lower pay?
findings.reason: Protime summary REC-0006 shows 0 unpaid absence days in January 2026.

findings.question: What do the emails claim, and how much weight do they carry?
findings.reason: DOC-0006 states 70% from 2026-03-01, consistent with approved REC-0002 (not applicable to January). DOC-0007 and DOC-0008 state a paid amount of 3500. DOC-0007 also says Piet worked full-time: that is an employee statement about hours worked, not the agreed regime, so it is deliberately not pinned as evidence. All are unverified emails: supporting at most, never authoritative.
